purpose: Re-validation of the v6.1.2 MPS survey legs (originally run on torch 2.13.0, an MPS-misread-affected build; see pystatistics docs/GPU_NOTES.md 'MPS strided-matmul buffer corruption'): identical curated cells (bench_categorical recipe, seed 20260617, m=20, maxit=10, method=auto, pystatistics 6.1.2 PyPI pin) fitted on MPS under the affected torch and under the mitigated nightly, both compared per column (pooled) and per chain against a torch-free CPU fp64-reference run of the same pin. Timings are contention-tainted (CPU reference ran concurrently) - do not cite as benchmarks.

findings.verdict: NO corruption fingerprint in the v6.1.2 MPS survey legs
findings.detail: The affected-torch (2.13.0, the build the paper's v612 MPS legs ran on) fits are statistically indistinguishable from the mitigated-nightly (2.15.0.dev20260813) fits on every metric, every cell, both repeats: pooled-vs-CPU TV max 0.035/0.043/0.002 (gss10k/gss50k/cses50k) under 2.13.0 vs 0.035/0.043-0.045/0.002 under the nightly; per-chain max deviations 0.14-0.22 in BOTH envs with matching distributions (that spread is legitimate chain-level Monte-Carlo variation, present on the clean stack too). No outlier chain appears under 2.13.0 that the nightly lacks.
findings.mechanism: Consistent with the misread's trigger profile: the corruption reproduces reliably on this machine/torch in the polyreg canary (batched (20,50,50) Hessian assembly from (20,50k,25) operands - deviation 42.9), but the curated GSS/CSES cells contain NO unordered columns, so polyreg never runs and the sweep's smaller logreg/polr/pmm allocations evidently never produce the triggering buffer placements under torch 2.13.0.
findings.scope: De-suspects the published v6.1.2 GSS/CSES MPS timing legs for these cells. Does NOT clear polyreg-bearing problems at survey scale on affected torches (the canary proves those corrupt), and does not affect the unrelated <=6.0.0/<=6.1.1 invalidations (penalty-bug era).
side_observations: MPS runs at n=50k are not bitwise reproducible at a fixed seed under EITHER torch (kernel-scheduling nondeterminism amplified by PMM donor selection); n=10k runs are bitwise reproducible. Chain-level spread between identical-seed repeats reaches per-chain TV ~0.18; pooled results are stable to ~0.002.

The CPU gss50k reference emitted at least one visible 'polr fit failed (ConvergenceError); using a marginal draw' fallback (Python warning dedup hides the true count) - first sighting of the 'polr grind' under 6.1.2, in the n=50k FULL config (m=20, maxit=10) that the 2026-08 audit only ran in cheap form (m=5, maxit=3, which converged 60/60).
